_provenance: DERIVED — a pure fold of the site's curated nav order into The Reading Path model (a dependency-ordered minimal way into the corpus). Node set and order are the site's; the why_before_next + stop_condition edges are authored. No wall-clock field — folds twice identical. Do not hand-edit; regenerated at build.
shape: ReadingPath(corpus) -> ordered [step]; each step = (what, why_before_next, stop_condition)
discipline: MINIMAL, not exhaustive — the smallest ordered read-set that reaches comprehension. For EXHAUSTIVE coverage-proof use https://loopmmt.com/corpus-manifest.json (the excavation layer).

steps.why_before_next: Establishes the one-line claim (an antifragile cognitive operating system using AI AND determinism) and the top-level map; every later page is a deepening of a claim made here.
steps.stop_condition: You can state, in one sentence, what Loop MMT claims to be and name the main areas the site covers.

steps.why_before_next: Unpacks the one-line claim into its load-bearing terms (antifragile, cognitive OS, determinism-plus-AI) so the history that follows reads as evidence for a stated thesis, not as anecdote.
steps.stop_condition: You can restate the thesis in your own words and name the terms it turns on.

steps.why_before_next: Grounds the thesis in the actual sequence — Minecraft redstone computer (2017) to the current system — so the apps and discoveries that follow have a chronology to attach to.
steps.stop_condition: You can place the major milestones in order and say roughly when the methodology itself began.

steps.why_before_next: Shows the shipped software the methodology produced — the concrete outputs — so the ideas register that follows is read against things that were actually built, not against claims alone.
steps.stop_condition: You can name several things Loop MMT shipped and what each one is.

steps.why_before_next: The ideas register — one card per worked-out idea — which is the conceptual inventory the Case then argues the purpose of; you need to know WHAT was discovered before reading WHY it exists.
steps.stop_condition: You can describe what the discoveries register holds and how it is organized.

steps.why_before_next: Document A — states why Loop MMT exists, who it is for, and what it will never become; this is the framing the corpus excerpt is then read inside.
steps.stop_condition: You can state the purpose the project sets for itself and the boundary it draws around what it won't be.

what.title: The Corpus — a first look — Loop MMT

steps.why_before_next: A first look at the real corpus behind the site (an excerpt of the Creed, the glossary) — the primary material the Knowledge Packs and Who pages assume you have now glimpsed.
steps.stop_condition: You can say what the corpus contains and point to at least one primary artifact (the Creed, the glossary) by name.

steps.why_before_next: Names the builder and the arc behind the work, and how to make contact — the human context that turns the corpus from an artifact into someone's project.
steps.stop_condition: You can say who built Loop MMT and how someone would get in touch.

steps.why_before_next: The published Knowledge Packs — self-contained references — are the deepest reading tier; reaching them last means you meet them already knowing the thesis, the history, and the corpus they draw on.
steps.stop_condition: You can describe what a Knowledge Pack is and report, from the whole path, what Loop MMT is, what it built, and how it holds together.

steps.why_before_next: An alternate front door for a journalist — what makes this different from other 'AI can code' stories; frames the same material for someone evaluating newsworthiness rather than adopting the method.
steps.stop_condition: You can state what the site says distinguishes this from a generic 'AI can code' story.
